name: obsidian-skills
description: Agent skills for Obsidian. Teach your agent to use Obsidian CLI and open formats including Markdown, Bases, JSON Canvas.
readmeExcerpt:
Agent Skills for use with Obsidian.

These skills follow the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) so they can be used by any skills-compatible agent, including Claude Code, Codex, and Open Code.

## Installation

### Marketplace

```
/plugin marketplace add kepano/obsidian-skills
/plugin install obsidian@obsidian-skills
```

### npx skills

```
npx skills add git@github.com:kepano/obsidian-skills.git
```

Instead of ssh, if you prefer to use https:

```
npx skills add https://github.com/kepano/obsidian-skills
```

### Manually

#### Claude Code

Add the contents of this repo to a `/.claude` folder in the root of your Obsidian vault (or whichever folder you're using with Claude Code). See more in the [official Claude Skills documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview).

#### Codex

Copy the `skills/` directory into your Codex skills path (typically `~/.codex/skills`). See the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) for the standard skill format.

#### OpenCode

Clone the entire repo into the OpenCode skills directory (`~/.opencode/skills/`):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/kepano/obsidian-skills.git ~/.opencode/skills/obsidian-skills
```

Do not copy only the inner `skills/` folder — clone the full repo so the directory structure is `~/.opencode/skills/obsidian-skills/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.

OpenCode auto-discovers all `SKILL.md` files under `~/.opencode/skills/`. No changes to `opencode.json` or any config file are needed. Skills become available after restarting OpenCode.

## Skills

| Skill | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| [obsidian-markdown](skills/obsidian-markdown) | Create and edit [Obsidian Flavored Markdown](https://help.obsidian.md/obsidian-flavored-markdown) (`.md`) with wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties, and other Obsidian-specific syntax |
| [obsidian-bases](skills/obsidian-bases) | Create and edit [Obsidian Bases](https://help.obsidian.md/bases/syntax) (`.base`) with views, filters, formulas, and summaries |
| [json-canvas](skills/json-canvas) | Create and edit [JSON Canvas](https://jsoncanvas.org/) files (`.canvas`) with nodes, edges, groups, and connections |
| [obsidian-cli](skills/obsidian-cli) | Interact with Obsidian vaults via the [Obsidian CLI](https://help.obsidian.md/cli) including plugin and theme development |
| [defuddle](skills/defuddle) | Extract clean markdown from web pages using [Defuddle](https://github.com/kepano/defuddle), removing clutter to save tokens |

aiSummary.oneLiner: A collection of advanced workflows and templates to maximize productivity and knowledge management in Obsidian.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository provides a masterclass in advanced personal knowledge management by offering a curated set of workflows, templates, and plugin configurations specifically for the Obsidian note-taking app. It moves beyond basic note-linking to demonstrate how to build robust, interconnected systems for task management, deep research, and creative writing. The project breaks down complex methodologies (like Zettelkasten or GTD) into actionable, step-by-step setups tailored for Obsidian's local-first architecture. By sharing these heavily refined systems, it helps users transform their digital notebooks into powerful, automated personal knowledge bases.
keyFeatures: Advanced Templating Systems: Provides complex, ready-to-use templates utilizing Dataview and Templater plugins to automate metadata and note creation.
Integrated Task Workflows: Demonstrates how to seamlessly blend daily task management (GTD) with long-term knowledge curation within the same vault.
Visual Knowledge Mapping: Offers configurations for optimizing Obsidian Canvas to visually organize research and brainstorm complex projects.
Plugin Orchestration: Guides users on how to combine specific community plugins safely and effectively to create synergistic productivity systems.
Metadata Architecture: Details robust strategies for structuring frontmatter to enable dynamic querying and dashboard creation across the vault.

useCases.title: Building a Zettelkasten
useCases.description: For researchers and writers wanting a structured, heavily refined setup to implement a frictionless Zettelkasten system for deep thought organization.

useCases.title: Automated Daily Reviews
useCases.description: For professionals seeking to automate their daily and weekly review processes by pulling tasks and notes dynamically using Dataview.

useCases.title: Project Management in Markdown
useCases.description: For individuals looking to manage complex, multi-phase projects entirely within Obsidian without relying on external task management apps.

useCases.title: Academic Research Tracking
useCases.description: For students tracking literature reviews, citations, and annotations within a heavily cross-referenced, searchable local repository.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This resource is for Obsidian power users, researchers, writers, and productivity enthusiasts who want to upgrade their vault architecture.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Browse the 'templates' directory to find specific workflows, and read the accompanying markdown files for setup instructions.
